messages:
Avani: quick heads-up — ran stackqa-mini onboarding for compact-embed-v2 with per-channel int8 quant and hit a surprising drop on very short queries (<=3 tokens). posting numbers below.
Liam: ouch, how big a drop?
Avani: fp16 baseline vs int8_pc
```
dataset: stackqa-mini (8k queries, short median=2 tokens)
model: compact-embed-v2
fp16  -> R@1: 0.742, R@5: 0.912, silhouette: 0.279
int8_pc -> R@1: 0.618, R@5: 0.894, silhouette: 0.148
cluster_purity(short queries): fp16 0.63 -> int8_pc 0.44
```
Maria: that's a pretty specific failure mode. did you L2 normalize before retrieval? short queries get squashed when quant noise is relatively large. :thinking_face:
Avani: yes normalization on both sides. tried cos and dot, cos still worse in int8.
Chen: two quick hypotheses: (1) quant noise is changing relative distances for very short vectors (few tokens -> low magnitude signal), (2) pooling differences amplify quant error. can you check mean-pool vs cls-token?
Liam: also try whitening / mean-centering on embeddings pre-quant — sometimes shifts help for micro-queries.
Maria: and compare per-channel vs per-tensor int8 (per-tensor usually slightly better for small-magnitude stuff), plus run a per-layer activation quantization sweep. maybe activations crossing zero exacerbate.
Avani: filing experiments now. priority list: mean vs cls, per-tensor quant, no-normalize ablation, whitened/centered, stopword-stripping for short queries. will run a small sweep overnight.
eval-bot: run registered: eval-pipeline v3.2 -> /runs/2026-03-19/1715550000-compact-embed-int8-sweep
Avani: command i'm running for reproducibility:
```
./scripts/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model compact-embed-v2 \
  --quant int8_pc \
  --dataset stackqa-mini \
  --queries "short" \
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,cluster_purity \
  --normalize true \
  --agg mean
```
Chen: small suggestion: add --seed 42 and --num-restarts 3, short queries are noisy.
Liam: if per-tensor fixes it, we may need a hybrid quant profile (per-channel for large layers, per-tensor for small projection heads). we should also check recall@k curve (k up to 50) to see if it's just rank jitter.
Avani: noted. will post updated numbers tomorrow. thanks for quick ideas. :thumbsup:
